rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Slide/lecture headers pass the squint test (names the concept) AND the truth clause (asserts what the body supports).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Epistemic mood ≠ punitive mood — student leaves uncertain about what's possible, not ashamed of what they did.

Slide 4 locates the failure signal in Claude's behavior ('hallucinating file paths', 'arguing with itself', 'missing a requirement'), not the student's, and frames stopping early as an operator's right to a readable result — matches the maintainer's 2026-08-01 rewrite (line 50: 'It's an operating rule, not a safety net').

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Lead with discipline, not failure mode — Big Ideas name positive disciplines, failure mode becomes the negative case the discipline addresses.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Headers lead with the discipline ('Every send-off is an experiment', 'Gap analysis...', 'Cancel is legitimate; traces are data'); failure-mode language (hallucinating file paths, arguing with itself, missing a requirement) appears only inside slide 4's body as the diagnostic tells for when to exercise the discipline, never as the header/title.
